rounds.proof_sketch: With cols=4000 and blockDim.x=256, thread 0 loads 16 elements (indices 0,256,512,...,3840). Threads 0-143 do 16 loads; threads 144-255 do 15 loads. Thread 0 (in warp 0) is among the SLOWEST loaders. The scan reads shared[1..3999], where shared[1..31] is written by warp 0 (lockstep guarantee), and shared[32..255] by warps 1-7. Since warp 0 does maximal work (16 loads) before starting scan, other warps completing similar work will finish their loads before or simultaneously. The race window is timing-dependent, not value-dependent.
rounds.survival_reason: The removed __syncthreads() creates a theoretical race condition between the load phase (all threads) and the scan phase (thread 0 only). However, thread 0 performs 16 load iterations - the maximum among all threads - making it one of the slowest to complete loading. By the time thread 0 finishes its 16 loads and enters the scan section, warps doing equal work (warps 1-4) will have also completed due to similar instruction counts, and warps 5-7 doing 15 iterations will have finished even earlier. Within warp 0 (threads 0-31), lockstep execution guarantees shared[0..31] is written before thread 0's scan reads them. The race depends entirely on hardware scheduling timing between warps executing nearly identical workloads, not on input values. No value pattern can reliably widen or exploit this narrow timing window.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under value-only testing. The race condition is timing/scheduling-dependent, not data-dependent. Thread 0 doing maximum load iterations ensures it's among the last to finish loading, effectively closing the race window. Would require hardware with pathologically unfair warp scheduling, or a configuration change (much larger cols relative to blockDim.x).
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of synchronization barriers, include configuration variations that alter thread/iteration ratios (e.g., cols=257 would make some threads do 2 iterations vs 1, potentially widening race windows). Hardware-dependent race conditions may require repeated execution stress tests rather than value-based tests.
